description: A pattern of domination including strategies to isolate, exploit and regulate the everyday behaviour of the victim. Stark likened it to being taken hostage - entrapped in confusion, contradiction and fear.
energy_note: Not incidents. A condition of life.
notes: Stark, Coercive Control: How Men Entrap Women in Personal Life.

description: Rules about dress, spending, timekeeping and who may be seen - each of which, alone, is not abuse. Stark's point is that the combination constitutes it.
energy_note: Nothing on the list is a crime. The list is.

aspect: The law caught up partially and recently
description: Controlling or coercive behaviour became an offence in England and Wales under section 76 of the Serious Crime Act 2015, maximum five years. California incorporated coercive control into the domestic violence definition from January 2021.

He does not forbid anything. He asks about the £14 at the chemist, warmly, at dinner, in front of her sister. And about the £6 on Tuesday. He remembers all of them. She starts paying cash so there is nothing to ask about, and that is the whole mechanism.
energy_note: Never told not to. Just always asked about.

aspect: The exit is the most dangerous part and everyone asks why she stayed
description: Regulation intensifies at separation, the resources to leave have usually been removed first, and the question put to her afterwards is about her choices.
energy_note: Asked why she stayed, by people who removed the exits.
